mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) reflects strong economic demand, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but SPX returns are negative in >40% of the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises >4% but SPX returns remain positive in >50% of the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month while FEDFUNDS decreases, it indicates inflationary pressures without sufficient monetary easing, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases >0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS decreases
failure_condition: If CPI increases >0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS decreases but SPX returns are positive in >40% of the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the 6-month moving average signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST rises >6-month moving average but SPX returns are negative in >40% of the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 jobs in a month signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases >100,000 jobs but SPX returns are negative in >40% of the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below the 3-month moving average signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS falls <3-month moving average but SPX returns are positive in >50% of the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) growth combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals supply chain disruptions and labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth <0.5% and UNRATE rises >0.2% but SPX returns are positive in >40% of the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises >4.5% but SPX returns are positive in >50% of the next 20 trading days.
